name: Education in the Elysian Concord
summary: Schooling stages, the school day, the curriculum floor, assessment, teachers, inspection, the Education Entitlement Account, institutions, libraries, and AI tutor constraints.

stages.name: Early support
stages.summary: Home-based, with health visiting and paid leave.

stages.name: Commune Early Years
stages.summary: Universal, free, play-based, delivered in the Commune.

stages.name: Foundation School
stages.summary: General education with no selection by ability.

stages.name: Upper School
stages.summary: Broad curriculum running to legal majority at 16 EY.

stages.name: Post-secondary and lifelong
stages.summary: Universities, technical institutes, apprenticeship, and adult learning, drawn from the Entitlement Account at any age.

schoolDay.secondWakingWeighting: practical work, craft, music, sport, and projects

curriculumFloor.name: Literacy in own language and Concordial
curriculumFloor.summary: Neither may substitute for the other, and no pupil may be taught only Concordial.

curriculumFloor.name: Numeracy in decimal and duodecimal
curriculumFloor.summary: Both bases, because duodecimal survives in the calendar, traditional measures, music, and ordinary speech.

curriculumFloor.name: Science including ecological literacy
curriculumFloor.summary: Enough to read the Ecological Commission's published account and understand what it says.

curriculumFloor.name: Civics: the five virtues and their conflicts
curriculumFloor.summary: Not instruction in loyalty but the study of cases where candour wounds, restraint paralyses, and redundancy competes with stewardship. Assessed on the quality of argument, not the conclusion.

curriculumFloor.name: History including the Concord's failures
curriculumFloor.summary: Four events appear in every regional curriculum without exception; a curriculum omitting any of them fails inspection.

curriculumFloor.name: Practical craft and repair
curriculumFloor.summary: Not vocational preparation but the civic virtue of repair taught with hands.

assessment.method: continuous portfolio assessed by the pupil's own teachers
assessment.rationale: A single examination is a single point of failure in a young person's life, and a system that concentrates a decision at one moment will eventually put a catastrophe there.

eighthTerm.name: The eighth term
eighthTerm.summary: Every teacher spends one term in eight outside the classroom on full pay with a funded substitute; compulsory, not a privilege.
eighthTerm.purpose: To prevent a profession that teaches about the world from losing contact with it.

teachers.disaggregationRationale: A measure attached to a person becomes a target for that person.

inspection.note: The one place Elysian education law gives a local body an absolute veto over a regional authority.

entitlementAccount.name: The Education Entitlement Account
entitlementAccount.summary: Twelve Elysian years of fully funded full-time study granted at 16 EY, drawable at any age in any increment for any subject, never expiring.
entitlementAccount.canonNote: Nobody goes straight from school to university as a matter of course. The median Elysian works or travels for eight years first and returns at 24 EY with an idea of what they want it for.

institutions.name: Technical institutes
institutions.summary: Applied, credential-granting, workshop-based; credentials of equal legal standing to degrees and staff on the same pay scale.

institutions.name: Research academies
institutions.summary: Postgraduate and specialist, attached to major facilities.

institutions.name: Commune learning centres
institutions.summary: One per Commune for adult, part-time, and community learning.

vocational.position: A civilization whose central project is maintenance cannot afford a status hierarchy that ranks knowing above doing.

libraries.purpose: Publishing everything is worthless if nobody can find it. The library network is the institution charged with making the record navigable, and canon does not claim this has worked, only that it is the attempt.

constraints.name: May not assess
constraints.summary: No AI-generated judgement contributes to any portfolio, credential, or moderation decision. Assessment is human, and this is a Concord floor.

constraints.name: May not complete work
constraints.summary: A tutor asked to produce the work must decline and offer to help the learner produce it; compliance is audited by sampling and failing vendors lose accreditation.

constraints.name: May not replace a teacher relationship
constraints.summary: Every learner under 16 EY has a named human teacher, and tutor availability may not justify raising pupil-teacher ratios. Three Regions attempted this in the EY 370s and were stopped by the Constitutional Court.

constraints.name: May not conceal uncertainty
constraints.summary: A tutor must be able to say it does not know and its confidence must be legible. Descends explicitly from the Cassian Incident: a system whose correct operation is indistinguishable from its failure is not safe to rely on.

knownWeaknesses.name: Portfolio comparability
knownWeaknesses.summary: Assessment without examinations is hard to compare across 34 Regions, so employers and universities lean on institutional reputation — reintroducing the signalling the system was built to avoid.

knownWeaknesses.name: Moderation integrity
knownWeaknesses.summary: The system rests on external moderators; moderation drift found in nine Regions and described as structural rather than incidental.

knownWeaknesses.name: Regional divergence
knownWeaknesses.summary: Attainment between strongest and weakest Regions differs by roughly two years of schooling; equalization narrows funding without closing outcomes.

knownWeaknesses.name: Teacher supply in small Regions
knownWeaknesses.summary: Persistent vacancies in Northreach, Austral Shore, and Highmarch; shared services are the mitigation and are criticised as centralization.

knownWeaknesses.name: The eighth term is unevenly honoured
knownWeaknesses.summary: 78% compliance; small schools cannot easily release staff and quietly do not.

knownWeaknesses.name: Private schooling
knownWeaknesses.summary: Only 2.1% of pupils and heavily constrained, but concentrated among high-wealth households and over-represented in some professions by a margin nobody has explained convincingly.

knownWeaknesses.name: Entitlement take-up skews
knownWeaknesses.summary: High earners draw 9.1 of 12 years, low earners 5.4. A universal right used most by those already advantaged.

knownWeaknesses.name: Status hierarchy persists
knownWeaknesses.summary: Technical institutes are legally equal and socially not; their graduates are under-represented in senior institutions and the gap has narrowed only slightly in two centuries.

knownWeaknesses.name: Late entry has costs
knownWeaknesses.summary: Mathematics, music performance, and some languages show measurably better outcomes with early intensive study, and the Concord has never resolved how to offer that without reintroducing selection.

knownWeaknesses.name: Institution concentration
knownWeaknesses.summary: Prestige clusters in about forty institutions whose graduates are over-represented everywhere; no mechanism has reduced this.

knownWeaknesses.name: AI tutor dependence
knownWeaknesses.summary: 11% of upper-school learners use tutors in ways that would fail the completion rule if the tutor were more compliant; enforcement is against vendors and the boundary is genuinely blurry.

knownWeaknesses.name: Library attention gap
knownWeaknesses.summary: 14% of access requests are library-assisted — a real contribution and nowhere near enough for the problem it addresses.
